prompts.text_original: As of October 2026, several General Authority Seventies were born in Europe. Pin a European country where a current General Authority Seventy was born, according to the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, six European countries are birthplaces of current General Authority Seventies: the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, France, the Netherlands and Portugal. Elder Massimo De Feo of Taranto, Italy, and Elder Hans T. Boom of Amsterdam are among them.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose king, queen or president was given a Book of Mormon, per the Church's country chronologies
prompts.text_original: A country whose king, queen or president received a copy of the Book of Mormon from Church representatives, as recorded in the Church's Global Histories chronologies
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Sweden, Netherlands, Costa Rica, Panama, Thailand, Slovakia
prompts.note: Scoped to the Global Histories chronologies read 27 Oct 2026; leaders of other countries have also received copies.
prompts.summary: Church representatives have often given the Book of Mormon to heads of state. The Church's country chronologies record gifts to King Oscar II of Sweden in 1897, the Dutch royal family in 1888 and 1952, Costa Rica's president in 1947, Panama's in 1961, the king of Thailand in 1968 and Slovakia's president in 1999.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: A copy of John Volker's 1888 Dutch translation went to the king and queen; Queen Juliana later accepted one after meeting David O. McKay in 1952.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Jan M. Sjodahl presented a copy to King Oscar II in 1897, his 25th year on the throne.

answers.name: Panama
answers.fact: Marion G. Romney presented a copy to President Roberto F. Chiari in 1961.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Ezra Taft Benson gave King Bhumibol Adulyadej an English copy in Bangkok in 1968.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: President Teodoro Picado was given a copy in San Jose in 1947.

answers.name: Slovakia
answers.fact: President Rudolf Schuster and his wife accepted a copy at a Church open house in Bratislava in 1999.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where US servicemen held the first Church meetings or were the first members (before 1955).
prompts.text_original: In several places the Church took root not through missionaries but through Latter-day Saints serving in the United States military, who were the first known members or held the first Church meetings there. Pin a country or territory where the Global Histories record this happening before 1955.
prompts.summary: Before formal missions arrived, Latter-day Saints in the US military often became the Church's first presence in a land. Two soldiers held the first service in Manila in 1898, and in World War II and after, servicemen's groups met in Costa Rica, Guam, New Guinea, the Marshall Islands, Puerto Rico, Korea and the Azores.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: First Church meetings in Korea held by US servicemen, 1945-47.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Soldiers George Seaman and Willard Call held the first service in Manila, August 21, 1898.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: First members on Guam were with the US military, 1944-46.

answers.name: Puerto Rico
answers.fact: Servicemen met in homes in the 1940s; 1953 meetings at Fort Buchanan chapel.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: First members in Costa Rica were US servicemen, July 1944.

answers.name: Papua New Guinea
answers.fact: Servicemen held services in New Guinea, 1944-45.

answers.name: Marshall Islands
answers.fact: First Church services held by American military personnel in the 1940s.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: Earliest known members were servicemen at Lajes Field, Azores, in the 1950s.
